findings.claim: There is no Darling of the Mob today because the committee agreed with itself almost nowhere. The Consensus Ratio (C5) has collapsed: the single most-supported name in the run carries 4 of 9 nominating seats. Removing Layer 0 did not produce breadth of conviction, it produced dispersion. 'nomination_count >= 2' is a threshold calibrated on a filtered pool and it was carried unchanged onto an unfiltered pool, where it now certifies far less.
findings.evidence: 9 distinct nominating seats appear in the brief (minervini, seow, weis, wyckoff, livermore, raschke, thorp, elder-lens, oneil). 32 nominations landed on the 18 qualifying names. Distribution: BBY 4 seats (max ratio 4/9 = 44%), GNW 3, nine names at 2, seven names at 1. 16 of 18 names (89%) are carried by two seats or fewer; 7 of 18 (39%) rest on a single seat. Across the wider run, 50 of the 164 universe names (30.5%) drew a nomination — roughly 1.8 nominations per nominated name. The 20-name cap did not bind, so nothing was competitive.
findings.what_is_owed: committee-desk chair and the PM: state what nomination_count = 2 is worth today versus under yesterday's longlist-AND-elder filter, and whether the qualification threshold should have moved when the pool it was tuned on was withdrawn. Do not answer by pointing at the count; answer by defending the constant.

findings.claim: The solo-high-conviction door handed seven of nine seats one private, uncorroborated name each. That is not the committee finding seven ideas; that is the rule bypassing the committee seven times. Every one of those names entered at conviction exactly 4 — the threshold value, never above it.
findings.evidence: Single-seat qualifiers, all at conviction 4: SLDE (oneil), BSBR (raschke), MDT (wyckoff), SPGI (elder-lens), TAK (livermore), CTVA (minervini), GME (thorp). Seven distinct seats, one name each, no seat used it twice, no entry at conviction 5. 39% of the deliberation set has zero peer corroboration of any kind.
findings.what_is_owed: committee-desk chair: show that a solo conviction-4 name and a two-seat name were weighed differently in deliberation, or say plainly that they were not. Each of the seven named seats: state what a second seat would have had to see to agree with you, since none did.

findings.claim: Sector breadth is an illusion. Financials is 39% of the set, Financials plus Healthcare is 61%, and not one name in the entire 18 sits in a sector the sector engine calls 'Momentum Building — Add'. The committee's apparent independence produced one concentrated bet on a fading group. (Sector trend state is a weak proxy on my menu and is never a supply-demand read — C10, C14 remain NOT_SERVED.)
findings.evidence: Financials 7 of 18: GNW, CB, MET, UBS, SLDE, BSBR, SPGI. Healthcare 4 of 18: JNJ, DOCS, MDT, TAK. sector_trend_state across the set: 'Momentum Fading — Hold, Don't Add' on 14 of 18 names (including all 7 Financials and all 4 Healthcare), 'Recovering From Weakness — Watch for Entry' on 3 (BBY, WELL, GME), 'Declining — Avoid' on 1 (CTVA). Zero names in an adding sector.
findings.what_is_owed: committee-desk chair and the PM lens: name the sector-exposure check that ran on this set, and if none ran, say so. seow specifically — you cited sector_trend_state as supporting evidence on BBY and WELL; explain how a sector state that reads 'Hold, Don't Add' or 'Watch for Entry' is a reason to add rather than a reason to wait.

findings.claim: Two seats produced 37.5% of the run's nominations, and their overlap is what manufactured two of the eleven multi-seat qualifiers. When the two most prolific nominators are also the only two backing a name, 'two seats agreed' is arithmetic, not corroboration.
findings.evidence: livermore 6 nominations in the set (GNW, CVX, VRNS, MET, JNJ, TAK), minervini 6 (BBY, GNW, CVX, JNJ, UBS, CTVA) — 12 of 32. CVX and JNJ each qualified on exactly those two seats and no others. By contrast oneil filed 1, seow 2, elder-lens 3, weis 3, wyckoff 3.
findings.what_is_owed: livermore and minervini: for CVX and for JNJ, state which part of your reason is not the other's reason. If the answer is 'the same BULLISH_BOS plus the same MA stack', the name has one supporter, not two.

findings.claim: The certainty challenge lands here, and it is mandatory. GNW is the densest agreement in the run — three seats, every one at conviction 4 — and all three recite the same two numbers. I hunted the hidden flaw and I found it: the most confidently held name in the packet is a shrinking business, in a sector the engine says not to add to, carrying two bearish divergences that no nominator mentioned.
findings.evidence: conviction sum 12 on 3 seats, average 4.0, the highest density in the set. livermore, minervini and raschke each cite day_vol 2.29 and each cite the same fib_618 stop 10.14 at 2.31% risk — one signal counted three times. Unmentioned by all three: div BEARISH with div_bear_count 2; sector_trend_state 'Financials / Momentum Fading — Hold, Don't Add'; rev_g -0.1086 and eps_g -0.2029 (revenue -10.9%, EPS -20.3%); fwd_peg 8.3802; rank 64, i.e. not a leader of the scored universe.
findings.what_is_owed: livermore, minervini and raschke, each separately: answer the two bearish divergences and the -10.9% revenue line, or withdraw the conviction-4. And answer C23 — what is the exact catalyst of change that forces the market to re-rate a shrinking insurer inside 12 to 36 months? A volume spike is not a catalyst.

findings.claim: BBY is the closest thing this run has to a mob darling, and its four-seat consensus is three readings of one field plus one seat who said it was not ready. The hidden flaw is in plain sight: the nearest structural target pays less than the risk taken, on a retailer with no revenue growth.
findings.evidence: 4 seats, conviction sum 12 (max 4). minervini, weis and wyckoff all cite the same contraction — was_squeezed True, vcp_tightness_pct 69.3, day_vol 0.79 — while seow explicitly downgraded it: 'entry 87.49 is +2.95% ABOVE ma_20 ... this is a watch, not a completed pullback' at conviction 2. Against that agreement: rr_tp1 0.74 (first structural target inside 1R), structure 50.5 and structure_shift RANGE (no break has occurred), rank 47, rev_g 0.0039 (+0.4% revenue), net_margin 0.0301, d/e 1.2985, lens.resistance 'warn'.
findings.what_is_owed: minervini, weis and wyckoff: three of you read the same tightness field. State the independent evidence each of you holds. And answer rr_tp1 0.74 as an entry question, not a stop question — why enter directly beneath resistance that pays 0.74R when seow, reading the same chart, says the pullback has not happened.

findings.claim: DOCS qualified as a two-seat name and both of its nominators wrote their own doubt into their reason. The threshold cannot tell the difference between two convictions and two shrugs, and today it counted two shrugs.
findings.evidence: conviction sum 5 (3 + 2), the joint-lowest in the set. elder-lens: 'No permission event ... this is my weaker trigger.' thorp: 'day_vol 0.33 says a third of normal participation, so the round trip is the unpriced cost ... Unwatched loss 14.83% of price sizes it small.' Independently: sma_dist 16.96% — the most extended name in the whole set — yet price 27.10 is still BELOW ma200 28.97; day_vol 0.33; rank 98; structure_shift RANGE; eps_g -0.1176.
findings.what_is_owed: committee-desk chair: DOCS and GNW both entered as 'multi-seat'. Show they were not treated as equivalent. elder-lens and thorp: you both hedged in writing — say whether you would defend DOCS in Round 2 or whether it entered on a count rather than on a case.

findings.claim: A break of structure that nobody turned up for is not a break, it is a drift. CVX is the second-most extended name in the set and its 'break' happened on below-normal participation, with earnings going the other way. This is the mirror of my own structural error: the committee is late here, not early.
findings.evidence: sma_dist 10.96% against the universe median 7.84 that oneil cited; structure_shift BULLISH_BOS on day_vol 0.84 — below-normal participation on the break bar; price 211.29 versus ma20 202.14, ma50 190.43, ma200 180.85; sector_trend_state 'Energy / Momentum Fading — Hold, Don't Add'; lens.coil 'warn'; rev_g -0.0464, eps_g -0.3186 (EPS -31.9%), fwd_peg -1.1243 on a negative growth input; no structural level passed the bracket gates (atr_fallback_stop 207.38).
findings.what_is_owed: livermore and minervini: name a defined confirmation or pullback trigger for CVX instead of a market entry 10.96% extended — for example a hold of ma20 202.14 on expanding participation. Advisory only; I do not block the name and I say nothing about the stop.

findings.claim: JNJ has the same defect as CVX and livermore already wrote it down, then nominated anyway. A seat that flags below-normal participation against its own break has stated the timing challenge for me; what is missing is the consequence.
findings.evidence: livermore, in his own R1 line: 'day_vol 0.92 is below-normal participation — noted against the break.' minervini's reason does not mention day_vol at all. sma_dist 6.61%; lens.insti_money 'warn'; sector_trend_state 'Healthcare / Momentum Fading — Hold, Don't Add'; pe 32.1884 on the FUNDAMENTALS line (brief line 100); no structural level passed the bracket gates (atr_fallback_stop 272.77).
findings.what_is_owed: livermore: you noted the flaw and did not price it — say what day_vol 0.92 changes about the entry, or say it changes nothing and defend that. minervini: address participation on the break bar, which your reason omits.

findings.claim: SLDE is the run's clearest case of buying the top of a move on one seat's word. Its own nominator wrote the word 'late' into the nomination. C22's Timing Delay Factor applies in reverse: my canon's error is acting too early, and a momentum book's error is exactly this.
findings.evidence: One seat (oneil, conviction 4). sma_dist 16.09% against oneil's own stated universe median of 7.84 and his own phrase 'late, not rejected'. day_vol 2.67 (+167% over its 20-day average) — participation is the reason to buy and the reason it is late. Price 24.73 versus ma20 22.55 and ma50 21.30. No structural level passed the bracket gates (atr_fallback_stop 24.00). fwd_peg -3.6653; the FUND NOTE records an IPO of 2025-06-18, so one full reported fiscal year underpins rev_g 0.365 and eps_g 1.9503.
findings.what_is_owed: oneil: define the pullback or confirmation trigger you would accept instead of a market entry 16.09% extended, and say what the one-fiscal-year base does to your group-leadership read. Advisory to the PM; this never blocks the name.

findings.claim: The catalyst check (C23) fails outright on GME, and it fails on the exact shape my canon is built to refuse: a cheap, broken, neglected name argued entirely on reward arithmetic with no stated cause of change. Cheap price alone is a trap. Neglect without a catalyst is a dead asset, not a bargain — and I never invent a catalyst from a chart.
findings.evidence: One seat (thorp, conviction 4), whose own reason concedes 'Only 2/5 momentum gates fire (flow, elder), so the stated reason is thin - discounted, not ignored.' The reason contains no thesis about the business at all — it is TP1 4.46R against 1.74R. Structurally the name is broken, not neglected-and-turning: structure 31.6, structure_shift BEARISH_CHOCH, sma_dist -5.29%, price 19.23 below ma50 20.30, ma100 21.64 and ma200 22.19; rank 131; rs IN-LINE with rs_spy_20d -0.6. Fundamentally: rev_g -0.0505, and the FUND NOTE states 'net_profit_margin 20.5% exceeds operating margin 10.6%: earnings are flattered by non-operating income.'
findings.what_is_owed: thorp: name the exact catalyst of change that forces the market to recognise this value within 12 to 36 months. If the answer is the reward ratio, that is a price fact, not a catalyst, and under C23 the trade is rejected. committee-desk chair: rule on whether an R-multiple with no thesis satisfies the framework-reason requirement.

findings.claim: A single seat carried into deliberation a name whose own sector state reads 'Declining — Avoid', named that caution itself, and qualified anyway. The rule let the objection through with the name attached.
findings.evidence: One seat (minervini, conviction 4), whose reason ends 'Caution named: sector_trend_state Declining - Avoid.' Also: structure_shift RANGE despite structure 91.6 (no break); price 88.64 above ma20 80.86 but ma50 83.23 sits ABOVE ma20 — the short stack is inverted; pe 58.702, fcf_yld 0.0106, div_yld 0.008123; no structural level passed the bracket gates (atr_fallback_stop 86.29).
findings.what_is_owed: minervini: a caution you name and then override is not a caution. State what overrides 'Declining — Avoid' here. committee-desk chair: say whether a self-declared sector veto should survive a solo qualification.

findings.claim: Four of the ten bracketed names in the set are being entered directly underneath their own first structural target, where the nearest thing price meets pays a fraction of the risk. This is an entry-timing observation about the target ladder as pre-entry information. I say nothing about any stop, bracket validity or gate — that is house law and I defer.
findings.evidence: rr_tp1 across the ten valid brackets: BSBR 0.05, WELL 0.28, MDT 0.48, BBY 0.74, VRNS 1.07, GNW 1.29, NFLX 2.47, CB 2.83, GME 4.46, DOCS 4.92. Four names sit below 0.75R to the first target. BSBR at 0.05 means the first structural resistance is effectively at the entry price of 6.02 while rr_tp2 is quoted at 2.75.
findings.what_is_owed: raschke (BSBR), seow and weis (WELL), wyckoff (MDT), and the BBY four: state whether your entry contemplates trading through the first target or taking partial profit at it, because at rr_tp1 below 0.75 those are different trades. Owed as timing, not as risk.

findings.claim: Withdrawing Layer 0 did not widen where the committee actually looked. Every qualifying name came from the two broadest source lists; the two narrowest sources contributed nothing at all. And the held book went unreviewed in this brief, with an internal count that does not reconcile.
findings.evidence: Source of the 18: longlist 13 (BBY, GNW, NFLX, CVX, VRNS, MET, JNJ, UBS, SLDE, BSBR, MDT, SPGI, CTVA), elder_list 5 (CB, DOCS, WELL, TAK, GME). qs (7 names) contributed 0; radar-premove (3 names) contributed 0. Separately, brief line 2 states 'held 2' while line 4 states 'Held book: BRZE, HNGE, V' — three tickers. None of BRZE, HNGE or V appears anywhere in the 18-name set.
findings.what_is_owed: committee-desk chair and the orchestrator: reconcile 'held 2' against a three-name held book, and state where the per-seat KEEP / TIGHTEN / EXIT-CASE lines for BRZE, HNGE and V are — the voice engine requires held names in the universe be reviewed on the same checklist, and if a held name is not in the universe it was reviewed by nobody. Also confirm the nominating roster: 9 seats appear in this brief and detect-lens appears nowhere, which changes the denominator of every consensus ratio above.

declarations: seat_role: CHALLENGE_ONLY — I do not nominate, I carry no vote in the tally, nothing above is a verdict, a conviction or a recommendation to buy. Severity of every finding is note or flag; none is a block.
template_a: NOT_COMPUTABLE — no sovereign, rule-of-law, exchange-control or debt-to-GDP input exists in this system, and it is out of scope for a US-equity book (C8, C13, C19, C24; R2).

template_b: NOT_COMPUTABLE — footnote and annual-report text are not served, so the Financial Statement Notes Ratio (C7) and step 3 of the five-step protocol cannot run. The brief served FMP ratio fields (altman_z, piotroski, pe, peg, margins, growth) and I read them only as corroborating context to a crowding or certainty claim, never as the footnote verification my canon actually requires (R3).

commodity_cycle: NOT_SERVED — no commodity price, input cost, production or inventory field exists, and the store does not hold the decades of history C14's 15-to-23-year cycle needs. gics_sector_name and sector_trend_state are cited as a WEAK SECTOR PROXY only and are never a supply-demand equation (C10, C14, C15; R9).
valuation_sanity: NOT_TESTABLE in canon terms — C21 wants book value, EPS and dividend yield as a three-filter sanity gate against primary filings; what is served is a vendor ratio row.

stop_position: DEFERRED_TO_HOUSE_LAW — C17's Consolidation Shakeout Filter is pm_override and does not govern. I have not argued against any stop, bracket, bracket validity or risk gate anywhere above. Where I cite rr_tp1 or an atr_fallback_stop it is as pre-entry timing information, which is what the field dictionary says the bracket is for (R7).
short_leg: OUT_OF_AEGIS_SCOPE — every bearish conclusion above (GME, CTVA, GNW) converts to a reason not to enter or a challenge to an existing long, never to a short or inverse expression (R8).

consensus_denominator: I counted 9 distinct nominating seats from the attributed R1 lines in the brief itself. The tally metadata was passed as attributed reasons with convictions rather than as an explicit seat roster, so every ratio above is computed against 9. If the true roster is 10 (detect-lens active but silent), every consensus ratio in this document is overstated and should be re-read against 10.

catalyst_check: no catalyst field exists on the deliberation record. C23 was asked of GNW, GME, CTVA and DOCS and answered by nobody, because there is nowhere for an answer to live. I did not invent one from a chart (C16, C23; R10).
engine_ask_1: pass the nominating roster explicitly, not inferred from attributed reasons — the Consensus Ratio's denominator is currently reconstructed rather than served.
engine_ask_2: add a catalyst / event field to the deliberation record so C23 can be answered rather than only asked.

engine_ask_3: recalibrate or re-derive the qualification threshold when Layer 0 is withdrawn — a constant tuned on a filtered pool certifies a different thing on an unfiltered one, and today it certified 7 uncorroborated names.

engine_ask_4: a news / filing text feed with a phrase-frequency counter, to unlock C9's Press Release Language Match and C18's 'It's Different This Time' metric. FMP already serves news and transcripts.
